result.question: How to implement the "Third Eye AI — Conversational Layer" (a voice-in/voice-out AI assistant for blind users, per the spec at github.com/sadeqisaidmohaddes-star/third-eye-ai-conversational-layer) WITHOUT training or building an LLM from scratch — i.e., using existing pretrained/hosted LLMs as the reasoning brain behind a voice pipeline (Pipecat + faster-whisper STT + swappable OpenAI-compatible LLM + Piper TTS, with Kyutai Unmute as a future migration target) — validated against current (2026) sources, flagging anything the spec's Option B gets wrong or outdated.
result.summary: Five angles split the question into: (1) the primary implementation path for wiring a hosted/self-hosted LLM into a real-time voice pipeline via Pipecat/LiveKit/Vocode; (2) the technical mechanics of STT-LLM-TTS streaming and sentence-boundary chunking for latency; (3) a comparative/pricing angle checking whether faster-whisper, Piper, and the recommended LLM choices are still the best mid-2026 options; (4) a practitioner/gotchas angle covering barge-in, tool-calling reliability, and swap-friendly architecture for a first-time small team; and (5) a recency angle hunting for post-spec frameworks (Kyutai Unmute/Moshi maturity, new open speech-to-speech stacks) and blind-accessibility-specific voice UX advances that could update the spec's Option B.
